title: Being typecast as a Dixieland player and playing in different styles
summary: Sessions could stamp a player as Dixieland; Dickenson played with Bechet, Lester and Eddie Heywood, likes any good music and feels at home in a couple of days.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: ...musicians, that helped them to get discovered, you know, just playing there. And you'd get stamped, too.

Like, "Dixieland Player" and so on; just cutting ...(?)... And it puts them really... People expect them to play this type of music, you know. So they're stuck with it. That's the type of jobs they get then, you know...
It's always sort of been interesting to me about you at a certain time in your career, when you were playing with Bechet and you played what some people might call Dixieland...
I don't like the word anyway. And then you turn around and play with Lester.
Right. But did they try to typecast you, too, and then...?

I was typecasted somehow as just Dixieland, you know. But I like playing. I like playing any kind. You know. If I like it, I like it. There's no... I don't discriminate on what's the type, if it's good.
You can also... I mean, you feel at home in almost any kind of musical situation.
Yeah. It don't take me long to feel at home. It takes a little while, I suppose, maybe a couple of
days to try to get into the swing and pick up that feeling that they have.
The rhythm is different in that.
